scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too much in this situation with my boyfriend. Let me start by laying out what's happening. I'm an atheist, and I'm in a relationship with someone who's been part of my life for three years. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. My son, who's 12, decided he wanted to play football on weekends. I was initially going to ask my boyfriend to help pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom, she told me it was my responsibility, not his. So I ended up paying for it myself, which meant I had to extend my work hours to 9 AM to 5 PM. Now, I needed someone to pick up and drop off my son on weekends because I'm at work. I asked my boyfriend if he could do that, but he looked uncomfortable and said he couldn't because he has his own things to do, like going to football games. I snapped at him, telling him that his dad lives in South London, which is a long way from where we live in North London, and that his dad doesn't drive. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small things like this for me. He got really angry and said he has to work longer hours to support me and my son, and he wants to use his weekends to chill and relax. He suggested we break up because I'm putting too many responsibilities on him. I was shocked and told him it's over a bloody football game, and I'm not the one out of line. My son went to my mom and had a heart-to-heart with her, which led her to call me and tell me I'm out of line. Now I'm wondering if I'm being too much (AITA) in this situation. So, to break it down, I'm asking for help with my son's activities, which I ended up paying for myself. I needed my boyfriend's help with transportation, but he refused, leading to an argument where I snapped at him. He felt burdened and suggested breaking up. My mom also thinks I'm out of line. I need to figure out if I'm being too demanding or if I'm just trying to manage my responsibilities. Maybe I should consider his feelings and whether I'm expecting too much from him. On the other hand, I'm handling the financial burden, so maybe I'm entitled to ask for help with logistics. I'm also thinking about the communication aspect. Did I handle the situation well when I snapped at him? Maybe I should have approached it differently, without making him feel guilty or pressured. Another point is the involvement of my mom. She's taking my son's side, which might be making things harder for me. I need to consider how family dynamics are affecting our relationship. I'm also wondering if the breakup suggestion was a reaction to the stress of the moment or if there's a deeper issue in our relationship. Maybe we need to talk about our expectations and responsibilities more clearly. In the end, I'm trying to balance my responsibilities as a parent with the expectations in my relationship. I don't want to be too demanding, but I also need support. I'm not sure if I'm overstepping or if I'm just trying to manage everything as best as I can.
